answer: The opal multiplier is published, charged in quartz, and raven lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1239 identities would post 2951 proofs and burn roughly 19 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
